articles.author: Faizan Akhtar
articles.description:
Summary


On October 8, 2026, WordPress security firm Patchstack disclosed CVE-2026-85097, a maximum-severity CVSS 10.0 flaw in Bricksforge — a popular add-on for the Bricks visual site builder used by roughly 6,000 websites. An unauthenticated attacker can upload and execute arbitrary PHP code on any vulnerable WordPress site: no login, no account, full site takeover. The vulnerability is a textbook trust-the-client mistake: the plugin validates a file's MIME type when it is first uploaded, but later trusts the file metadata the client's browser sends without re-validating it. And this is not theoretical — Patchstack detected active exploitation starting October 7, 2026 at 21:47 UTC, the day before public disclosure, from 63 unique IP addresses. If your site runs Bricksforge 3.1.8.9 or ol…
articles.title: CVE-2026-85097: Bricksforge WordPress Plugin Arbitrary File Upload Vulnerability — Analysis & Mitigation

articles.author: Faizan Akhtar
articles.description:
Summary


On October 12, 2026, GitLab shipped an emergency patch release — versions 19.4.2, 19.3.4, and 19.2.8 — to fix CVE-2026-97229, a maximum-severity CVSS 10.0 vulnerability in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server. No login. No account. Just a specially crafted regular expression smuggled into a CI/CD configuration, slipping past insufficient validation and tripping an integer overflow deep in the regex engine. GitLab itself is urging every self-managed installation to upgrade immediately — and this is the third regex-engine flaw in GitLab in a single month, after two CVSS 9.9 regex bugs patched on September 23. The pattern is unmistakable: attackers now know exactly which component of GitLab …
articles.title: CVE-2026-97229: GitLab CI/CD Regex Compiler Integer Overflow Vulnerability — Analysis & Mitigation
